facts.text: Maryland Park’s roots trace back to the Piscataway people, an Algonquian tribe that fished, hunted, and farmed along the Potomac before the 17th century.
Early land grants turned the area into a patchwork of rural estates along waterways, a pattern that lingered into the 18th century.
The Mid‑Atlantic climate keeps Maryland Park’s temperatures moderate, with continental influences softening extremes compared to farther inland.
Proximity to Chesapeake Bay keeps humidity high year‑round, sometimes turning mornings into misty, moisture‑laden scenes.
The Maryland flag, adopted by the state legislature in 1904, features the historic Calvert and Crossland coats of arms.
The flag’s design shows six gold and black vertical bars with a diagonal band in the first and fourth quarters, and a cross bottony in the second and third.
